report:
Typing in the Notes box was laggy because every keystroke re-rendered all the visible question rows, and each row does expensive regex work on every render. Moving the note state into the footer fixes it.

## Cause
`note` was `useState` in `ChecklistScreen`. Each keystroke re-rendered the whole screen, including the `FlashList`. That created a new `renderItem` and a new `onAnswer` function, so all 18 mounted `QuestionRow`s re-rendered. Each of those calls `riskLevel(item.title)`, and `riskLevel` builds about 6,000 `RegExp` objects per call (200 passes × 31 keywords). The profiler's CPU samples were dominated by `regExpConstructor` and `regExpPrototypeTest`.

## Fix
This is in `src/screens/ChecklistScreen.tsx`. I moved the note state, the input ref and the footer UI into a small `NotesFooter` component, and passed it as `ListFooterComponent={NotesFooter}`. Typing now re-renders only the footer. The screen and rows are untouched, and the UI looks the same.

## Before and after
Same scenario both times: fresh app launch, scroll to the bottom, focus the Notes box, then type `abcdefghij` at 150 ms per key. Both runs used the React profiler on a dev build.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| React commits ≥16 ms | 9 of 18 | 0 of 10 |
| Commit time per keystroke | 155–177 ms | all under 16 ms |
| `QuestionRow` renders | 162 (18 per keystroke × 9) | none of the 120 renders captured are rows (see below) |
| `QuestionRow` render cost | 1233 ms total | none captured |
| `ChecklistScreen` renders | 9 | none of the 120 captured (the profiler doesn't report per-component counts for clean runs) |
| Fiber renders captured | 2979 | 120 |
| `regExpConstructor` in CPU samples | dominant | none |
| JS thread idle during the typing session | not measured | 9253 of 9307 ms (99.4%) |

The 120 after-fix renders over 10 commits come to 12 per commit, which matches the footer's own subtree. The profiler only keeps per-component detail for hot commits, so the row counts above are inferred from that, not read directly.

I also checked that the footer behaves correctly. The counter shows "10 / 500". After I answered a question, which re-renders the screen, the note kept its text and the header showed "1 of 48 answered".

## Caveats
- These are dev-build numbers, which are roughly 3× slower than production. The ratio matters more than the absolute milliseconds.
- The baseline run captured 9 screen commits for 10 typed characters, so one keystroke was probably batched with another. The counts are what the profiler reported.
- I skipped native (Instruments) profiling, since the problem was on the JS side.
- `riskLevel` is still expensive and I did not change it. Answering a question still re-renders every visible row, so tapping yes/no will still show roughly the same ~150 ms commits. The sampling loop gives the same answer as a single check, so hoisting the regexes and dropping the loop would be a cheap, behaviour-preserving follow-up if you want it.

I stopped the simulator, debugger and profiler services for this device. Metro is still running since you started it.
